bAlthough the UL was not determined for arsenic, there is no justification for adding arsenic to food or supplements.
cThe ULs for magnesium represent intake from a pharmacologic agent only and do not include intake from food and water.
dAlthough silicon has not been shown to cause adverse effects in humans, there is no justification for adding silicon to
supplements.
eAlthough vanadium in food has not been shown to cause adverse effects in humans, there is no justification for adding
vanadium to food, and vanadium supplements should be used with caution.  The UL is based on adverse effects in laboratory
animals and this data could be used to set a UL for adults but not children and adolescents.
fND = Not determinable due to lack of data on adverse effects in this age group and concern with regard to lack of ability to
handle excess amounts.  Source of intake should be from food only to prevent high levels of intake.
Sources:  Dietary Reference Intakes for Calcium, Phosphorus, Magnesium, Vitamin D, and Fluoride (1997); Dietary Reference
